name: Great Hafir enclosure duct
summary: A water duct carrying water from the Great Hafir reservoir to the Great Enclosure at Musawwarat es-Sufra, a Kushite religious site in Sudan.
description: A water duct between the Great Hafir and Musawwarat’s Great Enclosure, part of the site’s local water-supply configuration.
tier_reason: A conveyance duct can be fine detail; its routing and phase are not identical to the reservoir basin. This is a scoped consequence judgement, not a reward for documentation or representation.

impact.note: One duct at one site, improving delivery of stored water to a single building complex, with nothing later known to rest on it.

date.label: by c. 350 CE (inferred)
date.basis: The project describes ducts to the Great Enclosure in the Meroitic use setting; their individual dates are not known.

events.statement: A duct from the Great Hafir is interpreted as supplying the Great Enclosure.
events.population: The Kushite Musawwarat religious-site water users and maintainers
events.caveats: The Great Hafir’s construction is radiocarbon-constrained to the 6th–4th centuries BCE; neither its original commissioning nor the ducts’ precise age is individually dated. The 350 CE endpoint is only a broad Meroitic contextual estimate, not a hard archaeological cutoff.

evidence.supports: The project describes the reservoir, 85 m inlet and water ducts supplying the Great Enclosure in its Meroitic context.
Dates the Great Hafir construction horizon and provides the Meroitic regional context.
